slides.title: Routing strategy: partner with RouteSprout now, and buy only on conditional terms

paragraphs.text: Routing strategy: partner with RouteSprout now, and buy only on conditional terms
Board pre-read for the March 2027 meeting · Should Atlas buy RouteSprout in 2027, and on what terms, rather than build or partner?
Atlas FieldOps
Board of Directors
Synthetic benchmark data · figures from the briefing pack or labelled team assumptions · $ in millions unless stated

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Do not buy RouteSprout on the proposed terms in 2027: partner now, and keep a conditional option to buy later at no more than $8.5M upfront
Neither acquisition path stays inside the cash limits once 18 months of operating losses are counted
–	Path A needs $22.0M against a $15.0M ceiling; Path B fits at signing but falls to $7.2M–8.2M, below the $9.0M floor
–	Nothing in the plan funds the $7.0M earnout due in 2029
The value case is overstated, and buying takes more than 15 years to pay back
–	$18.0M is 3.75 times recognized ARR, not the sellers' 2.5 times bookings
–	The $2.4M cross-sell is ARR, not EBITDA: net it adds about $0.1M a year, and loses $1.2M in the low case
Customer and execution risk is high and is not priced into the deal case
–	Churn rose from 12% to 21%, 41 accounts hold 58% of ARR and 30% of integration is unscoped, yet sellers assume 100% renewal
Only the partnership passes all four board criteria in 2027; building is affordable but late
–	At most $1.2M at risk, live this summer, no migration, and it out-earns ownership below about $3.5M of ARR
Buying stays possible, but only on conditional terms tested at a Q1 2028 gate
–	Partner now with first refusal; buy later for at most $8.5M upfront plus up to $9.5M if earned
–	Buy only if six thresholds clear; integrate via the API and pay nothing that breaks the cash floor

30% of the work is unscoped and the plan assumes zero change-management delay; API plus single sign-on (SSO) is simpler than migrating records and support

"2.5x recurring revenue" and $7.2M of "annual recurring new sales"

Value on QoE-verified recognized ARR only

slides.title: Sign the partnership on terms that cap cost, protect uptime and stop a competitor from capturing RouteSprout

paragraphs.text: 1 Cash    2 Value and payback    3 Customers and execution    4 Alternatives    5 Terms
Sign the partnership on terms that cap cost, protect uptime and stop a competitor from capturing RouteSprout
Commercial terms cap the cost and protect uptime
Protection terms stop a competitor capturing RouteSprout
▪	Scope and price (as offered): non-exclusive routing API with a $1.2M two-year minimum; gross profit splits 55% to Atlas and 45% to RouteSprout
▪	Ask, credit the minimum: count minimum payments against RouteSprout's 45% share, which cuts the $1.36M break-even and the $1.2M maximum loss
▪	Service level: at least 99.7% quarterly uptime, with service credits passed back to Atlas to match the credits Atlas owes its large customers
▪	Ask, segment exclusivity: exclusivity in utilities and repair contractors, Atlas's core segments; negotiate for it, but do not make it a condition
▪	Change of control: right of first refusal on any sale of RouteSprout, plus a right to terminate if a competitor buys it; the founders want to sell, so this is the key protection
▪	Pre-agreed purchase option: attach the conditional term sheet (p. 15), exercisable at the Q1 2028 gate, with partnership fees credited against the price
▪	Information rights: customer-level churn cohorts, the ARR schedule and pipeline data, which double as diligence evidence
▪	Continuity and roadmap: source-code escrow and data portability in case RouteSprout fails (EBITDA −$1.0M); share only interface-level roadmap, through a clean team
▪	Why walk away without them: the roadmap risk would then outweigh the speed benefit
Walk away if RouteSprout refuses first-refusal or change-of-control terms; reopen the build
Sources: Atlas FieldOps briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis

slides.title: In March, approve the partnership, fund diligence and set walk-away terms; decide on buying at a Q1 2028 gate

paragraphs.text: 1 Cash    2 Value and payback    3 Customers and execution    4 Alternatives    5 Terms
In March, approve the partnership, fund diligence and set walk-away terms; decide on buying at a Q1 2028 gate
Five decisions requested in March 2027
Sequence after approval
▪	Decline the $18.0M all-cash proposal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B)
▪	Approve the two-year RouteSprout partnership (at most $1.2M minimum) with the protections on p. 14
▪	Approve preliminary diligence: QoE, customer cohorts, integration scoping and key-person review; the CFO sizes the budget, which the pack does not give
▪	Mandate negotiation of the conditional term sheet: at most $8.5M upfront and up to $9.5M earned, with a set walk-away
▪	Defer the internal build, and revisit it at the gate if the partnership underperforms
▪	Apr–Jun 2027: sign the partnership; run diligence in parallel and negotiate the conditional term sheet
▪	Summer 2027: routing goes live with the enterprise prospects that asked for it; track attach and ARR
▪	Q3–Q4 2027: QoE and cohort results arrive; watch renewal outcomes for RouteSprout's 41 large accounts
▪	Q1 2028 gate: buy if all six thresholds are met (p. 16); otherwise continue the partnership, or start the build if demand is proven but the partner falls short
▪	Any time: if a competing bid emerges, apply the early trigger (p. 16)
Our reading: partnering in 2027, then buying in 2028, counts as one routing strategy
Sources: Atlas FieldOps briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); Team assumptions stated in the source analysis; team analysis
